1645639057.psych: Pre-commitment: the user sets an obstacle for a future temptation now, and the unlock friction breaks the scrolling automatism. Evidence: 'Works better than my willpower'.
1645639057.developer_type: small team (Labi, LLC, 5 apps on the account; estimate: a small company, not a factory)
1645639057.build_notes: iOS Screen Time API (FamilyControls, ManagedSettings, DeviceActivity) with the Apple entitlement; Android AccessibilityService/UsageStats; Safari content blocker for sites and Reels/Shorts; NFC; local analytics. 1645639057.hook: 'My screen time dropped from 7 to 3 hours because my phone makes me retype a paragraph every time I open TikTok.'

Loophole: changing the phone's time breaks the block (~1)
Can't unlock just one of several blocked apps (~1)

Daily limit on the number of unlocks

Hide the unlock buttons deeper in the app
praise: Really reduces screen time (often with concrete numbers)

6739782103.differentiator: Steps and water in one minimalist 'Liquid Glass' app with beautiful widgets and Apple Watch complications; an App Store Awards 2025 finalist.
specifics: Core mechanic: automatic steps + water reminders
What's shareable: widget aesthetics (estimate)
Social layer: none
Monetization: subscription or purchase ('costly to buy outright')
6739782103.psych: Small habits that are visible on a widget. Evidence: 'Sometimes the tiniest habits are the most important.' (description)
6739782103.developer_type: small team (Arkade Club Private Limited, 4 apps)
6739782103.build_notes: HealthKit/Health Connect, widgets, Watch. Biggest risk: step accuracy (mostly because of permissions).
6739782103.hook: 'The most beautiful steps widget you've ever seen.'
6739782103.monetization: Subscription or one-time purchase; prices not visible.
complaints: Steps aren't counted or aren't accurate (9)
Payment isn't clear before entering data (4)
Mandatory login (1)
6739782103.opportunity: The aesthetics are enough for growth; adding challenges with friends would bring virality.
6739782103.growth: 3.21 ratings/day since launch (2025-02-13, 606 days, 1,943 US ratings, average 4.64); reviews in 30 days: 40 vs. 19 in the previous 30 days. A young app, reviews doubled (40 vs. 19): accelerating growth, probably due to the award/featuring.
6739782103.marketing_evidence: No active ads in the US. Exact phrase 'GO Club' (34) only golf carts and unrelated advertisers; 'GO Club steps water' has no advertisers for the app.

6470828037.differentiator: A camera-based push-up counter (ARKit/Vision) with a '100 push-ups in a row' plan, seasonal challenges and a leaderboard of friends, country and world.
specifics: Core mechanic: automatic counting by camera, 4 modes (Sequence, Open Goal, Limit, Timer), personalized plan
What's shareable: posting workouts to Strava, trophies and medals
Social layer: leaderboard of friends, country and world
Monetization: subscription ~$3.99 monthly and a lifetime purchase
6470828037.psych: Competition and visible progress with a streak: records and rank give you a number to beat. Evidence: "the easy streak system made me enjoy it".
6470828037.developer_type: solo or small team (seller "wsfu", 3 apps; the description mentions an early version and waiting for feedback)
6470828037.build_notes: Pose detection (Apple Vision body pose / Google ML Kit Pose), backend for leaderboards, widgets, HealthKit/Health Connect, Strava API. Biggest risk: counting accuracy in poor lighting and from different angles.
6470828037.hook: My phone counts my push-ups and ranks me against all of America - day 1 to 100 push-ups in a row.
6470828037.monetization: Freemium; subscription ~$3.99 monthly and a lifetime option. In September 2026, Free Practice was moved behind the paywall, then partially restored after complaints.
complaints: Camera misses reps or freezes the counter (~9)
Features moved behind the paywall (~6)
Bugs during sign-up and login (~3)
No manual entry when the camera doesn't work (e.g. in the dark) (~2)
suggestions: Wider camera angle and low-light operation
Protection against accidentally ending a round (sweat on the button)
praise: Motivation and quickly fitting into a routine
Widgets, statistics and the lifetime option
6470828037.opportunity: More reliable counting and more exercises (squats, sit-ups), group challenges with friends and shareable rep cards; a stable, clear free tier.
6470828037.growth: 3,400 ratings over ~3 years (3.16/day); 10 reviews in 30 days vs. 1 - a spike, probably triggered by the paywall change (some of the new reviews are complaints).
6470828037.marketing_evidence: No active ads in the US. Exact phrase 'Push Up Counter' 1 result (National Bobblehead Hall of Fame, unrelated). The name is generic, the developer's name is unknown, so no developer search was done. The app has a tracking label, so ads outside Meta or via persona pages are possible (unconfirmed).

1508326506.differentiator: A mood diary where you draw your own emoji face of the day, so the calendar becomes a gallery of personal emoticons; adds a Pal companion and social reactions. Borderline: a diary, not a habit in the narrow sense; the seller has 9 apps.
specifics: Core mechanic: draw/pick the emoji of the day + a short entry, mood calendar and charts, rewards for checking in
What's shareable: widget and calendar with your own emoticons (estimate)
Social layer: reactions, follows and likes (from reviews)
Monetization: freemium + in-app purchases and ads for adding media
1508326506.psych: Self-expression and a long-term record about yourself: 'been tracking my mood for 3 yrs now! super cute widget'.
1508326506.developer_type: small company: EMMO Corp., 9 apps (estimate: a multi-product studio)
1508326506.build_notes: Canvas for drawing emojis, calendar and charts, media attachments and cloud sync, widgets, social feed. Biggest risk: data migrations (complaints about entries lost after an update).
1508326506.hook: 'I drew my face every day for a year - this is my year in emoticons.'
1508326506.monetization: Freemium, in-app purchases and ads to unlock photo/video; some users say the paid option is worth it.
complaints: Big update broke the layout, fonts and widgets (~7)
Entries lost after the update (~2)
Ads for adding images and a 'no ad to show' error (~2)
In-app purchases in a mood app, invite codes only for premium (~2)
suggestions: Bigger emoticons in the calendar, customizable widget
Full English localization (part of the interface remains in Korean)
praise: Drawing your own emoticons and personalization
A safe, private space to vent
1508326506.opportunity: Your own drawn emoji as a shareable 'year in faces' and a streak; stable migrations as a basic requirement.
1508326506.growth: ~12.4 ratings/day since 2020 (29,354); reviews 24 vs. 2 - a spike caused by a big update (mostly negative reactions).
1508326506.marketing_evidence: No active ads in the US. 'EMMO' 19 results, all unrelated (emmo.motion is an AI film creator, EMMA Kreativzentrum, gifts). The app has a tracking label, so ads outside Meta or via persona pages are possible (unconfirmed).
1508326506.reddit_notes: Wide organic mentions in mental-health communities (BPD, bipolar, ADHD, antidepressants) over several years; users praise the simplicity and cute design. Very positive tone, no traces of the developer or UGC ads.

6759581682.differentiator: An alarm that turns off only after you confirm a mission with the camera: push-ups, making the bed, hunting for an object or speaking affirmations, with streaks and badges.
specifics: Core mechanic: alarm plus a camera-verified mission, mission preview in advance
What's shareable: a video of the morning mission (estimate; not in the description)
Social layer: none
Monetization: subscription for smart alarms, paywall after the onboarding questionnaire
6759581682.psych: A commitment made at night, fulfilled in the morning; the physical action wakes you up. Evidence: "it literally won’t stop ringing until you finish a mission".
6759581682.build_notes: AlarmKit (iOS 26) or critical notifications, on Android AlarmManager with a full-screen intent; Vision for push-ups and object recognition. Biggest risk: alarm reliability (a missed alarm = 1 star) and verification without internet.
6759581682.hook: The alarm won't stop until I make my bed - look how fast I got up.
6759581682.monetization: Subscription (smart alarms require a subscription); prices not visible in the data.
complaints: Have to pay, paywall after the questionnaire (~7)
Alarm didn't ring, user was late for work (~3)
Mission verification doesn't work (connection error, object hunt) (~2)
Alarm rang without being set (~1)
suggestions: An exit from the lock when verification fails
praise: Really wakes you up (push-ups, making the bed)
6759581682.opportunity: A reliable alarm with offline verification and a free basic mission, plus a shared 'wake-up streak' with friends.
6759581682.growth: 685 ratings over ~221 days (3.1/day); reviews 2 in 30 days vs. 0 - the wave from TikTok promotion (reviews mention videos) has faded.
6759581682.marketing_evidence: No active ads in the US. Exact phrase 'Nooze' 4 results, all unrelated (Pet Passion 'SNOOZE', Bears with Benefits, algorx). Meta Ad Library is empty, but reviews point to paid marketing (e.g. TikTok or Instagram ads).
6759581682.reddit_notes: No mentions on Reddit in Google results; hits are about general alarm apps and an unrelated site, nooze.news.

1541027222.differentiator: An app blocker that doesn't ban but adds friction: a delayed open that grows with each open, an 'Is this important' prompt, a scroll interruption and locking of its own settings. Everything key is free, plus a streak for respecting limits.
specifics: Core mechanic: a pause before opening a distracting app (escalating), limits per day and per app, strict block by time or number of opens, a streak of days without exceeding limits.
What's shareable: the drop in screen time and streak length (a review mentions streaks of 500+ and 400+); there is no visible sharing mechanism in the app (estimate).
Social layer: none in the app; spreads by word of mouth ('I've put over 7 friends on').
Monetization: free, with a donation or lifetime premium (mini-games instead of scrolling).
1541027222.psych: Friction breaks the muscle-memory automatic opening, and the streak adds fear of loss: 'prevents opening certain apps out of muscle memory'.
1541027222.developer_type: solo or small team (ScreenZen LLC, 1 app, no tracking label; reviews note the developer listens to feedback)
1541027222.build_notes: iOS: Screen Time API (FamilyControls, ManagedSettings, DeviceActivity, shield screen) with the Apple entitlement; Android: UsageStats + AccessibilityService (Google Play policy risk). Minimal backend. Biggest risk: fragility of the Screen Time API after iOS updates (already visible in reviews) and entitlement approval.
1541027222.hook: I put a 30-second wait before every Instagram open, here's my screen time after 7 days.
1541027222.monetization: Free; voluntary donation or lifetime access to premium features (price not visible in the data).
complaints: Bugs after an iOS or app update: the 'Open' button doesn't respond, crashes in settings (~3)
Blocks without warning or also blocks apps that weren't selected (~2)
Can't delete apps, constant re-syncing (~2)
'Not free' because part of it is behind payment (~1)
suggestions: Reliable warning 5 minutes before a block
A clear 'stop' signal when the user bypasses a limit
Keep it simple instead of adding complex new features
Choosing the session length when opening an app
A mode without a timer (only a pause/friction before opening)
Comparison with OneSec - users ask for a similar 'pause' approach
praise: Free, yet more effective than Apple Screen Time and paid competitors (~10)
Highly customizable and hard to bypass (~5)
The open counter and the streak keep users honest (~3)
1541027222.opportunity: Add a social layer for Gen Z: a shared streak with a friend, a shareable 'hours reclaimed' card and a weekly duel for who scrolls less; a subscription for social features with a free core.
1541027222.growth: ~26.9 ratings per day over ~5.2 years (51,441 ratings); 150 reviews in 30 days vs. 0 in the previous 30 days (probably a data gap, estimate). Steady organic growth driven by word of mouth.
1541027222.marketing_evidence: Only 2 active ads in the US (screenzen.co), both launched 8.10.2026 - one its own, one a creator partnership; a test, no sustained campaign.
1541027222.reddit_notes: Strong organic presence for years (nosurf, digitalminimalism, ADHD communities), the free model is constantly praised; the developer actively responds to feedback. Tone is strongly positive, with criticism that the friction works only temporarily.

6751820866.differentiator: Self-discovery as a game: levels of questions get deeper and deeper, a small creature guides you, and the app combines answers into a profile of patterns (attachment, self-sabotage, thinking).
specifics: Core mechanic: quizzes and quests by level, journal prompts, insights that adapt to the user, a companion creature.
What's shareable: personality insights and a 'constellation' (estimate; format like a personality quiz).
Social layer: not in the data.
Monetization: subscription after a 3-day trial, paywall in onboarding.
6751820866.psych: Identity and curiosity about yourself, packaged as progression through levels. Evidence: 'This makes reflection feel easy and not forced'.
6751820866.build_notes: Designing the question bank and levels (most of the work is content), LLM for synthesizing insights, animated creature, account and sync. Biggest risk: quality and 'accuracy' of insights; without a psychologist it comes across as generic.
6751820866.hook: 'In 10 questions this app explained why I sabotage relationships.'
6751820866.monetization: Subscription with a short trial; those who stay pay, but the paywall in onboarding triggers 1-star reviews.
complaints: Short trial and a paywall that can't be skipped (~5)
Insights can't be read or scrolled (~2)
Loss of account and data (~1)
Freezing in onboarding (~1)
praise: Precise and deep insights about yourself (~6)
6751820866.opportunity: Add shareable insight cards and comparison with a friend/partner (compatibility) as a viral layer; free first levels before the paywall.
6751820866.growth: Launched 12.2.2026, 908 ratings, ~3.76 ratings/day; reviews in 30 days 2 vs. 3. A solid start without a tracking label, many mentions of therapists.
6751820866.marketing_evidence: No Innie advertisers in the US (48 results, all unrelated).

6760232059.differentiator: An alarm you can't turn off until you photograph a specific object in your home, and after waking up it guides you through an affirmation and a short meditation instead of scrolling.
specifics: Core mechanic: a photo mission (find and photograph an object) to turn off the alarm, a system alarm via AlarmKit (rings even through silent/Focus)
What's shareable: a video of the morning 'hunt' for the object (estimate, no built-in sharing)
Social layer: none
Monetization: hard paywall (~30 USD according to a review) before setup
6760232059.psych: Upfront friction: the user schedules a physical task for themselves that gets them out of bed: 'You literally cannot snooze it's so great for me.'
6760232059.developer_type: Solo developer (estimate): an individual, Oduduabasi Victor, 4 apps.
6760232059.build_notes: AlarmKit (iOS 26) for the system alarm, on Android AlarmManager + full-screen intent; on-device object recognition (Vision/ML Kit, comparison with a reference image), affirmations and short meditations (audio content). Biggest risk: alarm reliability on Android and false object recognition.
6760232059.hook: POV: the alarm won't stop until you find the toothbrush in the bathroom.
6760232059.monetization: Hard paywall, ~30 USD mentioned; prices not in the data.
complaints: Have to pay before anything else (7)
Alarm rings at a random time (1)
suggestions: Free basic tier before the paywall (derived from complaints)
Louder sounds are more effective (user tip)
praise: Really gets you out of bed, no snooze
6760232059.opportunity: Keep the photo mission, but add morning streaks, a friend who sees whether you got up on time (accountability) and a free first level; move the paywall to after the first successful morning.
6760232059.growth: 2.72 ratings/day (559 ratings over 206 days) - a fast start for a new app; reviews in 30 days: 1 vs. 6 - slowing down after the initial wave.
6760232059.marketing_evidence: No active ads in the US. Exact phrase 'BeYou': 230 unrelated (BeYou Showroom, BeYou Medical Spa...); 'BeYou Alarm': generic alarm advertisers, none of them this app.
